messages:
Jordan: Heads-up — I hit a case where safetensors shards with compressed headers break our fast probe and later cause an OOM when the loader mmap()s the file.
Anya: Ugh. Which probe are you running? the 4-byte magic check?
Jordan: Yep. Current probe does a tiny read at offset 0 (8 bytes) and if magic doesn't match we fall back to a manifest scan. Gzipped headers show 0x1f8b so we misclassify and then downstream path assumes full-index layout.
Sam K: Can we do a multi-offset sample instead? e.g. sample offsets [0, 256, -4096] and look for either safetensors magic or index tombstone markers.
Anya: That helps for many cases, but each extra GET is ~2x cost on S3. 3 reads per shard will hurt cold-start throughput in high QPS.
Matt P: Proposal: implement a safety-net probe window: try 1 small read at 0; if inconclusive do a second read at 2048; if still unknown do a single-range GET that returns header+trailer (bytes=0-2047 and last 4k) so we cap to 2 HTTP range requests in the worst case.
Jordan: Also: use posix_pread / ReadAt for the probe path instead of mmap to avoid committing address space and touching pages in the probe. That keeps resident size small during classification.
warmup-bot: note: warmup budget=50ms/shard under load. Multi-read probe will be gated by warmup budget for hosted tier. :alarm_clock:
Anya: Encrypted shard case: header magic is opaque. For encrypted blobs we should prefer manifest/registry metadata first rather than blob sampling.
Sam K: Agreed. Idea: set a small ingest-time flag 'probe_safe' in the weight registry when we know the header is plain. Metadata read is much cheaper than blob ranges.
Matt P: Nice — ingest-time flags + per-namespace fallback policy. On Dedicated we can be more aggressive; on Hosted we follow budgeted probe strategy.
Jordan: Telemetry: add metrics probe_attempts_total, probe_http_ranges, probe_fallback_to_manifest, probe_time_ms. Example log line we should emit:
```
PROBE shard=abc123 outcome=inconclusive ranges=2 time_ms=18
```
Anya: Add unit tests for gzipped-header and encrypted-header cases. Also cache probe outcomes in the hotloader for TTL=5m to avoid repeated sampling on high-traffic shards.
Sam K: One more operational detail: KV cache warmup asks for layer offsets. Probe should either return a small layer map or a 'defer-layermap' signal so warmup doesn't prefetch full layers blindly.
Matt P: I'll sketch an RFC addendum with algorithm pseudocode, cost estimate (range reads per cold start), and rollout plan (canary on Dedicated then staged Hosted).
Jordan: Thanks — if folks +1 I'll follow up with the patch and a short load-test.
Anya: +1 :thumbsup:
Sam K: +1
warmup-bot: scheduled warmup-canary/dedicated for 3427779999
